resources.string: A tall Human man stands before you as you enter into an impressive building with polished granite floors and marble pillars that seem to ascend endlessly. You know this place to be a Triptych Expedition Corps’ hub, one of three dotting the familiar lands of home, and a place of promise and adventure.

“Hail, contractor, and welcome to the Expedition Corps,” greets a tall Human man, his steel-plated armor decorated with a self-consuming, sapphire-colored oarfish. “I am Thaddius Cantor, Marshal of this post, and I have been tasked with familiarizing you with the task at hand,” he says with a big, almost excited, grin. You know you are about to leave everything you know to be familiar behind in favor of a life of riches, glory, and excitement. As Thaddius loops around a great, finely carved, mahogany desk (the only real piece of furniture in the room, strangely enough), he extends his left hand to shake yours with vigor. “I know not where you came from or what you’ve done in your previous life but it was certainly enough to catch the gaze of the Triptych,” he says with a hint of jealousy, though not malicious in its nature. “As they might have told you before sending you here, the primary duty of ‘dusters’ is to act as a leader for a small expeditionary force to uncharted lands. It’s not easy by any means and there’s sure to be trouble but you seem like the type of person capable of handling it,” Thaddius muses, shifting slightly to motion to the desk behind him where maps and several documents lie. Several poorly made, rather nondescriptive, maps lie splayed out over the rich dark wood alongside letters that comprise a handful of dossiers that illuminate a number of organizations, workers, and potential threats that lie ahead of you. As Thaddius begins to brief you there’s a swimming sense in your head that tends to come from an informational overload and your brows furrow. Thaddius takes note and chuckles lightly. “If this is all proving to be too much at one time, fear not. In the pack you’ll receive with standard supplies there is a sending stone which will allow communication between us even at the farthest reaches of the world! Day or night I will be available to offer aid as best I can,” he assures you. “You’re not in this alone.”

Your briefing after the fact is, well, brief. A ship comprised of tradespeople, farmers, warriors, and supplies awaits you and though you are the first officially commissioned Triptych contractor to be sent to the large island that awaits you, Thaddius takes time to warn you that you are not the first person to arrive. Small bands of pirates, Orcish ronin, and others have taken to the lawless land and await you there and as you set sail the next day, sending stone in hand, you find yourself content in knowing that you’ll match any challenge that comes your way with courage, valor, and perhaps the benefit of a little luck.

“Welcome to the Island!” Thaddius’ voice booms through the sending stone with an almost manufactured level of excitement. “My recommendation is to craft a name for it yourself. Perhaps when this is all over the Triptych will use the name you give it,” he says with glee. “I’ll not tell you what needs to be done, though I recommend you familiarize yourself with the facilities at hand. Take time to visit your crafters, builders, and non-combatants. Perhaps you might join them in short missions to help establish your outpost; after all, they don’t call you ‘dusters’ for the jackets you wear,” Thaddius jokes. “Whatever you choose to do, it might be wise to aid your farmers to get an early supply of food going for your outpost. It should go without saying but a steady supply of high-quality food will not only ensure the survival of those you lead but also empower you to take on greater challenges!”

“Ah, I see you’ve chosen to aid your gatherers. Fantastic choice,” Thaddius praises over the sending stone. “Contrary to what many nobles and wizards believe back home, these hard laborers are some of the most important people there are. A steady stream of ore, fish, wood, and crops will allow you to keep your forges burning, your bellies full, and your buildings standing. The supplies you gather can be given over to your crafters to create new weapons, armor, and improvements to your outpost to ensure your survival is all but guaranteed.”

“There’s nothing like hard work to really invigorate your soul, is there? It’s like my father once said: The Call’s greatest song is not from the piano or cello, but from the sound of a pickaxe striking stone or an axe on a tree,” Thaddius says, an almost somber tone transmitting through the sending stone. “The supplies you’ve gathered have many uses and you should consult with your crafters to see what can be built, or what is needed further, with the supplies you’ve gathered. If you’re certain you don’t need them then perhaps the merchants in your outpost’s inn would be interested?”

“Supplies are fantastic to have but they’re almost useless if there isn’t someone around to shape them into something useful. Your expedition has a number of skilled tradespeople that can help you shape the bounties of the land, sea, and air into things that will aid you in your journeys. Each requires different things that you might encounter while abroad so variation on how you spend your time gathering is advised,” Thaddius encourages. “If you find yourself in need of extra supplies, the merchants at your inn will offer up some of the product gathered by trading with locals and the Triptych for a price. While I am not particularly fond of selling needed supplies for a price, I suppose they have their needs as well.”

“Nothing can be done well on an empty stomach. Shrimp and potatoes will offer up excellent dining early on but I would advise you not to ignore how important your expedition’s cooks truly are! Not all food is made equally and rarer, more difficult to acquire, ingredients will create better dishes. Food has such a rejuvenating quality and can often make the impossible seem possible. Before any venture into dangerous lands I recommend you pack as much food as you can. It could save not just your life but those of your expedition.”

“Now that you’ve made landfall I advise you to make contact with your farmers. They’ll likely need some help, umm, ‘processing’ some of their livestock,” Thaddius says, seemingly uncomfortable with the word “slaughter” for some peculiar reason. “In the past I’ve heard of animals becoming quite ornery after the passage and establishment on new lands so this could be a good opportunity to test your combat skills. I recommend you bring some food, though if you don’t have any I’m sure you’ll have some things to cook after.”

The farmhand, a tall Orc woman, bows low in thanks and sends you on your way with some coins and some of the spoils of your “processing” venture. As you begin to head back to the outpost you dwell on how hostile, almost malicious, the animals were and you begin to recall a very uneasy feeling that settled over you as soon as you arrived at the farm that you can only identify as some type of old, dark, magic that permeated the place. As you consider all that has happened so far you begin to wonder if the animals were truly so “ornery” because of the move and the new environment or perhaps something more wicked is at play.

“Hah! I’m glad to know our Duster on the island can handle a few angry chickens!” Thaddius laughs. You think you might have detected some measure of nervousness in him as you explained the odd and ominous feeling that you felt during your time at the farm. “Very odd, indeed, though I am unsure what to make of it. Please let me know if you observe this feeling again and I will call upon whoever I can to identify it. Until then, I recommend you cook some of the fruits of your labor and prepare for whatever might come next.”

As your outpost is unfurling and establishing itself, word begins to reach you that some residents are experiencing very odd encounters with small, mischievous, creatures in the night. Some report being awoken by a forceful tug on their hair or minor acts of destruction throughout the outpost. Perhaps most damning, however, is the meddling with local crops. You know, from the description of the creatures seen, that they are imps and since they often build elaborate subterranean hives you know there’s likely a cavern nearby. As you ready a raiding party you know that these imps, however largely harmless they might be in the moment, could prove to be a detrimental nuisance in the future.

“Hail, Duster! Good work in tracking down those dastardly imps. I agree that the correct course of action is to root them out as best you can, though I’m sure you know it’s much harder to get rid of an imp infestation than many would believe. Nevertheless, I have faith you and your valiant warriors will root out the issue sufficiently.”

As you strike down the last of the imps, and the giant rats that grew fat on their stolen bread, you feel a sense of satisfaction wash over you. You know that it’s never this easy to root out imps from their hives but the work you’ve done today will ensure your townsfolk will go unbothered by their ilk for at least a little while. In the cavern as you drove into the depths you noticed some peculiar treasures snagged by the imps. Rusted swords, shields, and a few crates with Goblish, the guttural language of Goblins, crudely painted on them. It becomes clear that imps are not the only nuisance you’ll have to deal with. You’re unsure what the relationship between the imps and the Goblins is, but it cannot be good for your outpost.

Seemingly agitated and stirred by the activity on the island, a population of isolationist Goblins has been stirred up like a hive of angry wasps. Goblins on their own are not particularly dangerous but can become quite deadly in groups. These are not the civilized, scientifically and magically gifted, Goblins of Naithea’s great mountains but rather an odd enclave that has seemingly regressed, enraptured by some sort of presence that you cannot yet identify. The odd Goblins have begun to climb out of their warrens and hidey-holes to attack hunters and explorers alike and, though there haven’t been many deaths just yet, a few victims have reported falling extremely ill after surviving the attack which has left many concerned about poisoning or worse.

The battle was harder than you expected it to be. The Goblins, and the giant rats they kept like hunting hounds, fought recklessly and with little regard for their own lives, which is highly unnatural for any Goblins you’ve ever heard of. As you raid their cave base you discover a rudimentary lab and the corpses of several giant spiders that you deem to be the source of the poison that coated their weapons. You find yourself wondering why the Goblins would employ the use of poison for any reason OTHER than to harass and kill your people. What’s worse is that that feeling of ancient and wicked magics sank into you for a time in the Goblin cave: an unnatural presence you can’t shake. Once you make contact with Thaddius, he agrees with you. “It’s not like Goblins to so senselessly use poison… They’d never use it for hunting, at least not in their right minds. I would recommend you seek out the source of these great spiders. Moreover, I will make it a point to try and make contact with the Goblin Hierarchs to see about any missing trading teams or the like that might have ended up on the island.”

As your people recover from the Goblin raids it becomes clear that the Spider’s poison, inflicted by those Goblin attacks, is far deadlier than anticipated. Your outpost’s healers believe that an antidote for the poison can be synthesized from the venom glands of several spiders alongside the Broodmother’s fangs, which are believed to be exceptionally potent, though you remain somewhat unconvinced this will work. As you gear up to track down the spider’s den you begin to hear rumblings of outpost guards being attacked along the perimeter of your outpost and beyond by individuals adorned like wealthy pirates. These “bandit-pirates,” as your guardsmen have begun to call them, are not a great danger yet, though you decide to double up patrols in order to prevent anything dreadful from happening while you’re out slaying the spiders in their lair.

With the Broodmother felled, for the time being, and the reagents acquired to try and synthesize a cure for their venom you take a brief moment to search the antechamber of the Spider’s immense den nestled in a cavernous tunnel structure below a gargantuan, overturned, tree. The wild monkeys that nested in its branches, driven as mad as the spiders by the island’s strange presence, have finally gone quiet. The antechamber is filled with all manner of horrors, though most notably, wrapped in thick layers of webs as if they were packed away for later consumption, you come across the bodies of bandit-pirates, strange black-robed and hooded figures from another group that radiated the unfamiliar and ancient magic you’ve felt before, and an Orcish ronin adorned in once-finely crafted armor now rusted and in disrepair. The hooded figures and the ronin bring concern to you as you realize there’s much more on the island than you initially thought and the presence of lawless Orcish exiles could prove to be exceptionally dangerous.

“Duster,” Thaddius calls to you with a discernible layer of concern echoing in his voice. “Thank The Call so few suffered from the native spider’s venom. After reaching out to the Goblin Hierarchs I could not track or locate a population of Goblins that has gone missing in recent memory. Moreover, after consulting with an Arcanologist, I cannot seem to track down what kind of magic you’re detecting on the island. I’ll not bore you with the full report but judging by the island’s position along mapped ley lines there should not be much greater than a latent arcane presence. All this to say there must be a powerful source on the island. I encourage you to explore more and report your findings. As for these bandit-pirates, I recommend you do what you can to drive them out as soon as possible. They’re likely to be more dangerous than the Goblins and imps.”

Thaddius was correct in asserting the bandits likely weren’t difficult to track down. In a sizeable compound deep in the thick jungles you and your forces descended upon them. The bandits and the rogues who ran with them fought hard but you fought harder, and as you cornered the bandit leader, he refused to be slain by the likes of you. He withdrew a vial of the same poison found in the Goblin cave and drank it, dying shortly after, manifesting an odd connection between the Goblins and the bandits that one might not have assumed existed before. As you begin to rummage and loot through the bandit supplies you encounter a small lockbox which radiates that disquieting magic. As you force the lockbox open a handful of keepsakes catch your eye: the badge of a Triptych expedition, an ornate key-shaped stone that looks as though it were torn from obsidian with an empty slot shaped to fit some sort of gemstone, and a letter written in an unfamiliar hand that seems to be the source of this power. As you open the letter to read it the message is clear. Someone, or something, drew the Goblins and the bandit-pirates into an unholy alliance and supplied them with purpose: to kill you and wipe out your outpost. Signed below is some sort of symbol you know to be of Orcish origin followed by the letter “K”.

As you return to your outpost to brief Thaddius on all that has transpired and question him about the Triptych badge you found, you feel an unnatural and entirely uncommon chill in the air. Seemingly the moment you find yourself crossing into the confines of your outpost a commotion erupts from the eastern edge of your outpost. You rush over with your cohort to make sense of the screaming and shouting only to be met with a most unwelcome sight. It appears that in an attempt to excavate near your outpost, builders stumbled upon and gradually unearthed the entrance to something unlike anything you or your allies have seen thus far. At first glance the entryway unearthed was crafted of polished stone in a way that conveyed some type of reverence; however, the creatures that spilled out from within were not creatures of divine benevolence. The undead, skeletons and zombies and all other manner of rotting horrors, made their presence known and shambled out to slaughter your people and raze your outpost. As you ready yourself to dive into the “crypt” you begin to sense that same sickening presence that you could feel at the farm where your journey began and attached to the letter that seemed to burn in your pocket. You know now that whatever answers you seek may very well linger in the Undead Crypt. You and your party ready torches and dive into the darkened depths to seek those answers and stymie the flow of cursed undead or die trying.

Exhausted, lightly wounded, and covered in viscera, you and your cohorts battle your way through the reanimated corpses of Orcs, Humans, and Dwarves bedecked in armors of various makes and kinds. You can’t be certain but you could swear somewhere along the carnage you saw an Orcish zombie wearing armor that looked similar to that of the First Orcish Empire, ruling much of the known world nearly a thousand years ago, but the implications of that seemed rather difficult to parse out in the moment. Zombie after zombie, horror after horror, you and your cohort carved your way into the crypt until you found its heart. Within the heart of the crypt the wicked and vile magic you’ve been feeling was nearly overwhelming but as you power through and see what lies before you the pieces begin to fall together. A circle of ebon-robed necromancers chants and channels their sickening spells to reanimate the dead found within the crypt and command the corpses to destroy you. As you descend into the heart of the crypt and put an end to them, fit with whatever means you may have to ensure the bodies do not arise again, you realize now that the overwhelming stench of necromancy and its magical presence has been what you’ve sensed since your first day on the island. All at once it becomes clear the reason the animals on the farm were so anxious and violent stems from the presence of the most sacrilegious magic on the island and that whoever this “K” character might be they are almost certainly a necromancer themselves.

As you take the time to digest all that you’ve seen and learned, a subtle draft relieves your nostrils of the mustiness and rot of the crypt and reveals to you a lightly cracked open hidden passageway door most assuredly absentmindedly left cracked by one of the necromancers you and your party slew. As you nudge open the door you stare into the seemingly infinite blackness of a tunnel where that draft you noticed originated. As you and your party follow the passage back a faint light grows brighter and brighter with each step until you meet a rusted iron gate that leads into the courtyard of a dilapidated cobblestone fortress. The ramparts crumbled underneath what seemed like a century of rainfall and jungle encroachment and the overgrown courtyard felt almost like an extension of the consuming flora found deep in the island. As you stand at the threshold between the crypt and the fortress beyond you can hear the sound of faint voices and the clattering of supplies echo off the long-abandoned walls. You realize that whoever this “K” individual might be they very well might be in this fortress or, at the very least, whoever instigated the undead attack on your outpost might be present to answer for their crimes. Whether you return to your outpost to resupply or press on now, you know that it’s only a matter of time before they realize what happened in the crypt and mount another attack or flee.

As you and your force muster your strength to raid the shattered halls of the ruined fortress it becomes very clear that the hearths found within are not the only things dead. As you move your way up through the tunnel and into the courtyard you are met with a counter force of more undead monsters though this time they are adorned in rusted, torn, and otherwise nearly destroyed pieces of armor from the first armies of the Triptych. These creatures are the reanimated remains of Triptych guards, knights, and wizards, the last of them now slinging the same dark magic as the necromancers of the crypt, and their presence here makes sense of the Triptych badge found in the bandit chief’s belongings. As you fight your way through the stronghold you begin to notice tattered Triptych banners, crates marked with Triptych symbols, and the remains of a long-abandoned outpost just like yours. The focal point of the fortress, a great keep at its center, barely stands and through one of the collapsed walls you spy your target. A twisted, malformed, physically imposing Orc raises his hands high into the air as a well of sapphire flames bursts from his fingertips and threatens to cascade over the entire courtyard with you in it. As you dive behind a nearby pillar and feel the icy flames dance around you a booming, gravelly, voice echoes through the courtyard. “You! Leave this land and you, too, may benefit from the shattering of our mortal coil. Remain and join the ranks of those who have been felled by Kur’zul!” the Orc threatens. As you peer around the corner you see the Orc raise up his left hand as he releases a near-deafening whistle. The air crackles with the sound of coldflame flickering around you and in the distance, growing with each second, a raucous noise of leathery wing flaps can be heard. Overhead a fledgling green dragon swoops down low and in an instant the Orc that identified himself as Kur’zul is caught by the dragon. As the beast flies to the north you can see the shrinking figure of the Orc climb atop the beast like someone else might a loyal steed.

With the Fortress Ruins cleared, at least for the time being, you begin to take account of what supplies can be taken from the once-stable bastion of Triptych power. As you navigate into the formerly great keep of the fortress you find a hall on the second floor, once used by the commander of the fortress for planning, that Kur’zul had clearly been using as an operating base. Upon investigating the Orc’s left-behind belongings you discover correspondence on small pieces of parchment, the most important of which reveals to you that a small stronghold of Orcish ronin is hidden within the thick jungles of the island to the north. These Orcs, unbound from their oaths of servitude to the Orcish Imperator of Callarax, seem to have some sort of loyalty to an Orc Khan of the past called Kargral the Arcane and have pledged to protect Kur’zul so long as he “rewrites the legend of Kargral.” You find this very concerning though, perhaps, find it more concerning that whatever is truly happening, has happened, and maybe will happen on this island is shrouded to you. As you collect the parchments, a few tomes which carry an aura of necromantic magics around them, and whatever supplies you might need, you begin the journey back to your outpost with one goal in mind: answers.

Thaddius’ voice over the sending stone seems to betray any sense of confidence or joviality that you might’ve believed he possessed beforehand. He doesn’t interrupt you, nor does he attempt to explain himself or the Triptych but instead simply listens to your account in full before speaking. “I am… sorry, Duster, for the deception. The truth is as you say. A century ago, when the Triptych first was formed, each of its nations pooled its best and brightest explorers and researchers to cast out an expedition to the very island you stand upon. It was the first of what was hoped to be many expeditions to places of great significance to the First Orcish Empire and its rulers. The island was believed to possess immense magical power by the legendary Khan Kargral the Arcane and became his obsession if the legends are to be believed. The Triptych did not put much stock into the legend but desired to see what Kargral might have left on the island centuries ago,” Thaddius explained. “The first expedition, the one that built that fortress, was led by an Orcish wizard named Kur’zul who was, at one point, the Imperator’s personal advisor in all things magic. When he volunteered for the mission the Triptych thought nothing of it; however, within a month of the expedition landing on the island, communication was lost. Smaller scouting parties were sent to the island, though they never returned, and the Triptych began to believe the island was cursed in some capacity or, perhaps even worse, Kur’zul had rebelled and sought to craft his own nation. Eventually the situation was buried out of fear of diplomatic disaster,” Thaddius admitted. His voice was low, perhaps cautious, as he explained to you. “For Kur’zul to still be alive… his power must be great,” Thaddius mused before clearing his throat over the sending stone. “I know my word means very little to you, Duster, but know I am truthful when I say that is all I know. Moreover, I have decided that I will personally travel to your outpost to aid you in putting this matter to bed. If you can find it within yourself to at the very least accept my aid, I assure you I shall make up for any deception.”

You’ve gathered everything of importance that you took from Kur’zul’s haunt and laid it out next to a map your scouts have hastily compiled of the island. In an area largely unexplored north of the volcano at the island’s heart is a place of dense jungle, climbing into the northern mountains, that could, based on constraints of topography, likely be the spot of whatever enclave is supporting Kur’zul. As you and your strike force begin preparing to strike out, you recall a time in your youth when you were told legends of great Orc warriors who, either in reality or fiction, faced off against numbers far greater than themselves and left bloodied and victorious. These warriors often wore scaled armor and wielded single-sided curved blades that are renowned for their sharpness and strength. Even in an era of firearms and siege weaponry many a commander might quake at the idea of facing off against a small force of Orcish warriors. These “ronin,” as they are often referred to, are exiles or defectors from Callarax City and are extremely dangerous alone, and only The Call knows what other enemies you might face. As you trudge your way through the jungle and around the volcano you cast your gaze up to see dragons along the western shelf of the mountain and, for a moment, it feels as though they are watching you too. As you begin to discern the great wooden walls of a makeshift stronghold in the distance you steel yourself for what comes next.

To say that the fight was hard would be an understatement. As you and your cohort charged through the gates of the Orc Stronghold, so arrogantly left wide open for your assault, you were met with a small force of highly trained and skilled ronin. The legends told of their prowess were true, and yet years of living undisciplined, cut off from society, seemed to whittle down not only the ronin’s edge but also their sanity. They did not fear death and so they charged in with recklessness that very easily could have overwhelmed you but you held strong. The greater challenge was the lumbering Mountain Trolls, re-animated and stitched together from mismatched parts, that stood between you and the inner sanctum. As you cut down the last and burst into the stronghold’s makeshift sanctum, Kur’zul was kneeling, surrounded by a circle of runes that radiated the shadows of necromancy and death magic, before raising his arms high into the air. In his right hand he clasped a spellcasting focus that looked something like the “key” you found after clearing out the bandits’ base what felt like a lifetime ago. “You are too late, Triptych pawn! I will conquer life and death themselves!” he cried out in a mixture of anticipation and glee before the world around him split open. In an instant he was swallowed up by a portal. You claim victory over the Orc ronin today but you can’t be certain what comes next. All you know as you begin to collect what supplies you can and rally your troops is that you must find a way to track Kur’zul no matter the cost.

As you return to your outpost your guard captain informs you that a Triptych ship containing a small number of reinforcements and a Human named Thaddius has arrived. Bewildered by the speed of their arrival you travel to meet Thaddius at the small inn meant to house traders from beyond the island. Thaddius stands near the bar in full regalia, boiled leather armor and light chainmail painted with the symbols of the Triptych, with a mithril longsword sheathed at his hip and a large mithril kiteshield leaned up against the bar beside his left boot. As you enter he bows his head. “Duster, it is good to see you again,” he says in an almost sheepish manner. “I am glad I was not turned away at the docks. I know I have much work to do to regain your trust. As such I am here, on behalf of the Triptych, to aid you in whatever way I can,” he says. “The trip to the island was short thanks to the squad of battlemages provided to me by the Arcaneum of Lyonia, though as they manipulated wind and sea for our journey it occurred to me that perhaps, with their aid, we might be able to parse out the nature of Kur’zul’s wicked plot. With your permission and supervision I would provide them a glance at those grimoires you retrieved from the ruined Triptych fortress.”

The four battlemages wore heavy adamantite plated armor etched with intricate runes and magical patterns that seemed to shimmer in the light. Their long ocean blue cloaks trailed behind them and filtered up to face-obscuring hoods which covered just the top of their faceless masks. You know these warriors to be elites of Lyonia’s Arcaneum, its magical university and research center, and know that their presence at your outpost means the Triptych understands the threat Kur’zul represents. As they each peer over the grimoires and tomes taken from Kur’zul’s lair, one speaks up. “The necromancer seeks to breach the Realm Between and gain entry to a place he only refers to as the ‘ancient temple.’ In one entry of his journal he recounts a portion of the legend of Kargral which describes the Khan’s desire to break the cycle of life and death so that he may control even who lives and dies eternally. In this venture, the legend says, Kargral converted his once-opulent home into a temple meant to serve as a place to honor himself when he ascended to godhood. The necromancer believes that Kargral, in part, succeeded and that his temple now exists beyond this realm in the Between,” the battlemage briefed in an entirely monotone voice born of extensive emotional-control training. “By channeling power into a focus crafted by Kargral, one can follow him, it says.” “I suppose we must thank Kur’zul for translating and discerning the list, then,” Thaddius said, a fraction of his jovial attitude returning as if to lighten the mood. The battlemages did not find him entertaining.

“The molt of a great and old dragon and the ‘Essence of the Mountain,’ which can be derived from the antechambers and tunnels of the volcano, must be used in unison to peer beyond our realm and into the Realm of Chaos. There, if the notes are to be believed, one must collect the Eye of Chaos from a great infernal sanctuary,” Thaddius said. With each word his tone grew more and more worried until he sounded outright panicked. One of the battlemages clarified, “The molt of the dragon and essence of the mountain are reagents to create a gateway to the Realm of Chaos,” as if that made the tasks any less momentous. Thaddius dismissed the battlemages then and drew your attention to a map nearby. “You mentioned you spotted dragons on your way to the ronin stronghold, so I’d venture that is as good a place as any to try our hands at collecting a molt. I would wager that the ritual will not simply take any dragon’s scales, however, so I think no whelp’s shedding will do,” he said with a certain severity in his tone. “As for the mountain’s essence, I have to believe that there is some sort of manifestation of the volcano’s great elemental power within the antechambers that wind along it. Whatever aberrations might guard it are sure to be a challenge for us.” As he speaks you realize he means to join you and your cohort on these tasks. Whatever you may think of him he seems desperate to make up for his deception.

To plunge into a volcano in search of elemental power sounds like the plans of a raving madman but by this point, after facing off against all manner of creatures both living and dead, you might as well be mad. Thaddius rallies your troops and you begin the trek towards the small volcano at the center of the island and, upon drawing closer to the mountain than you have been before, you begin to see more and more dragons of all sizes circling above. They don’t seem to be hostile but you do know they can grow terribly territorial should you draw too close to their nests. “Such incredible beasts,” Thaddius remarks during your ascent along a path which winds up the side of the volcano, “I must admit I do not very much look forward to facing off against them,” he says with a bleak tone. Your ascent was as easy as it could possibly have been given the circumstances, though, as you stand at the precipice of an expansive cavern, you hear so audibly the crackling of fire, and beneath it the baying of hounds, from the dark depths below. You’ve never faced off against demons before but you prepare yourself and begin your descent.

Demons are not easy foes to face off against and those that nest in the heart of a volcano are regarded as some of the more difficult and dangerous. As you descend into the depths the hellhounds and lesser demons seem wary of you and your cohort at first though quickly begin to lash out at you, leaping up from crackling streams of lava, in heavy waves of intense heat and fury. By some miracle of The Call both you and Thaddius manage to only sustain a few burns here or there but not all of your warriors are so lucky. As you follow the winding pathway into the volcano you find yourself in an immense antechamber somewhere unknowably deep within the mountain and, at its center, the bright orange glow of what you surmise to be the Essence of the Mountain radiates out from the gemstone’s place on a pile of rubble. The closer you get to your prize the fiercer the demons become though the waves abate and retreat once you finally reach it. Thaddius grapples at the thing, no larger than the palm of his hand, and struggles to lift it. “By The Call!” he swears as he has to use both of his hands to lift the gemstone and slip it into a pack which weighs him down further. You do not envy the trek he has ahead of him though at least it seems the demonic tide has abated.

As you and your party exit the hellmouth Thaddius slumps down at the edge of the cave, muttering something under his breath about the impossible density of the magical gemstone. A path winds down to your right though you notice that, to your left, a craggy pathway winds further upwards in the direction towards the shelf where you and your soldiers have seen dragons circling about. You realize that it would likely be beneficial to make your way up to collect the molt of the dragon. Thaddius seemed almost defeated when you revealed to him your plan to follow the path though he sighed and gathered up a small force of warriors who had traveled alongside him on his journey to the island and entrusted the Essence of the Mountain to them before setting them on a journey back to your outpost. As they trudged down the path back home, making plans for who would carry the stone when, Thaddius let out a sigh of relief. “They should not be harassed on their way home… I must admit some joy at the thought that I will not have to carry that burden further.” Your entire group takes a few moments to collect themselves before beginning the journey along the volcano towards the dragon’s shelf.

Almost every household back home tells stories of the primordial and ancient dragons, said to have shared the world with the ancient Maltheites as the first creatures on Myora, as the joining of primal power and timeless regality. These great, scaly, beasts are functionally ageless and most commonly die from disease or lack of suitable food in the area of their clutch which results in their expansive spread throughout all of Myora despite their presumed low population numbers. Dragons are rarely, if ever, observed in the wild and seem to possess culture and intelligence all their own which no anthropologist or biologist has yet discerned. This is because dragons are inherently distrustful and oftentimes hostile to outsiders that aren’t obviously their food. You remember all of these “fun” facts as you stand at the precipice of their lair, riddled with the bones of animals and the armored remains of knights presumably from the previous expedition. Some of those knights have begun to stir with the island’s necromancy, and lesser demons that clawed their way up from the volcano’s depths skulk among the bones. Above, whelps and adolescent green drakes begin their descent to intercept you. This will not be easy.

Many heroic legends back home end with a warrior’s battle, and eventual triumph, over a great and powerful dragon but those stories made it seem much easier than it actually is. The dragons did not seem to have been on the island very long and though the whelps understood the risk and backed away as your party entered their lair, some of the more bold drakes lashed out, joined by the risen knights and lesser demons that harried your flanks. Tail whips, fiery breath, wing buffets, and all manner of ferocious and surprisingly swift attacks threatened to kill you, Thaddius, or your warriors but you stood strong. In a lull between battles you spotted your prize, a length of discarded dragon’s leather at the mouth of a sizeable cave on the shelf, and as you rushed towards the molt the drakes and their attacks waned. They withdrew from the mouth of the cave just as you remembered that dragons only begin their molting when they’ve reached their prime adulthood and are, as many have theorized, at their strongest. As you remembered this, an immense black dragon erupted from the shadowy depths of the cave to gnash at you. The beast’s ebony scales, noticeably different from the forest green scales of the dragons you saw outside, radiated with primal magic in a way that made the air oppressive and weighted. It reared back its razor-filled maw, with five rows of dagger-sharp teeth, and prepared a fiery cascade as you gathered up what you could of the molt and turned to make your great escape. The torrent of great, purple-tinted, flame erupted from the beast and licked at your calves as you and your forces sprinted across the shelf and, as you reached the entrance, you realized the awakening of the “king” Black Dragon struck fear not just in your crew but in the dragons themselves. They did not pursue but, in truth, you did not linger to see if they would.

The trek back to your outpost was one of silence, reflection, and caution. None of the dragons flew from their lair to pursue you and the volcano did not erupt with the force of furious demons. Instead, for the first time in a long time, the island felt calm despite your better knowledge. Exhausted, flame-scarred, and mourning in silence the loss of comrades, your troupe trudged back along the pathway through the jungle until you arrived back at your outpost. You speak at length with Thaddius about the plan but ultimately decide it’s best to get some rest for the evening, deciding to begin anew in the morning. When morning comes you gather up the things you’ve collected and a new batch of loyal warriors to take your first steps towards the next phase of your pursuit. “It seems so rudimentary but Kargral’s tome specifies that the Essence of the Mountain must be encased in the Molt of the Dragon and then lit aflame with an immense bonfire. Apparently this creates a portal to the Realm of Chaos…” Thaddius sighs, raising his left hand to thoughtlessly stroke at his mustache, before turning his gaze to you. You nod and do as the Khan’s tome suggests: wrapping the dense gem in the magically charged dragon’s discarded scales and setting it at the base of an unlit pyre. At your signal someone sets the pyre ablaze and you watch as the flames dance upwards, filled to the brim with uncertainty, prepared for whatever comes next.

The great pyre burns bright and hot only for a second before the flames begin to lash out in all directions, taking on a sickly yellow coloration with flecks of sea green and pink, before linking and forming a burning gateway into a realm beyond. Despite the raging flames you feel as though you can enter and not be burnt. As you draw closer and closer you realize there is, in fact, no heat radiating from the gateway and you motion your cohort to follow. Despite his reservations Thaddius follows suit with unmatched resolve. As you cross into the gate, within the timespan it takes you to blink your eye, you find yourself in a structure composed of what appears to be, at first glance, a densely packed crimson brick with otherworldly “seashells” baked into it like some sort of unsettling coquina. You thank The Call or whoever is listening for the fact that the Realm of Chaos has breathable air and sally forth to meet whatever it is that lies ahead. The hallways of otherworldly coquina wind and twist in ways that seem impossible before they lead in a vague “down” direction. As you descend these stairs “down” you realize your only path leads down into a pool of still water.

As you cautiously lower yourself into the water you are very suddenly transported into a wide-open field. The sky above you is golden in color and three sapphire-colored suns burn overhead, though they don’t seem to radiate heat and the “grass” that surrounds you, colored in a violet hue, stands still in the presence of no wind. Ahead of you, ringed by the crimson battlements of the stronghold, a lone tree, the size of a building, with hundreds of blinking eyes stares directly at you and your arriving cohort. Just then creatures erupt from the ground below and charge forth in a nearly indiscernible horde of incorrectly placed hands, feet, hooves, and frothing maws. As you ready your weapons you call out to your cohort that the “tree” is your destination and charge forth to face off against whatever these creatures might be. As they close the distance the shapes resolve, if only barely, into things you recognize: demons, hellhounds, and towering fire giants, each one warped by Chaos into something that should not exist.

With each Chaos-warped demon that fell, a loud screech erupted from the great “tree” just ahead, and as their blackened blood, which smelled of roses and radiated a citrine blue glow, began to coat whatever wicked soil made up the ground beneath your feet, you felt emboldened to continue. Once you finally made it to the base of the tree, all of its hundreds of eyes stared down at you with a mixture of disdain and curiosity. Thaddius pressed his back to yours as he panted in exhaustion laced with fury. “Whatever we need to do, I suggest we do it now!” he cried out as another mass of demons and hellhounds began to gather on the horizon. As you stared into the largest of the eyes you could see on the tree, the gaze seemed to change in some way, as if it had deemed you worthy, and just then a fleshy and bloody maw began to open slowly. Nested on a tri-forked tongue-like appendage was a rough pearl not entirely unlike the pearls found on the shores back home. As the horde of demons, hounds, and fire giants stampeded forward, Thaddius muttered a prayer to himself before roaring out commands to your troupe, expecting this to be his final moments, as you reached out to collect the pearl. The moment your hand closed around the thing you were… home. Back at your outpost with Thaddius still at your back roaring in a mixture of fear and anticipation for battle with the rest of your surviving cohort. As the realization of where you were settled in to those around you and the shocked murmurings of the civilians around you began to pierce through the pounding of your heartbeat in your ears, you open your hand and peer down to see the rough pearl-like stone you had collected from whatever that “tree” was. It dawns on you, then and there, that the “pearl” was responsible for your teleportation and that this was the prize you sought: the Eye of Chaos.

After much-needed recovery from traveling beyond the pale you reconvene with Thaddius and lay everything out before you. Kargral’s tome was unclear as to what happens after one ventures into the Realm of Chaos, which frustrated Thaddius, who muttered repeatedly “Damned Khan…” and “I bet he didn’t even travel to that nightmare!”, and confounded you. The pearl lay on a small cloth next to the tome, the letters from Kur’zul, and the key you found in the bandit leader’s lockbox. As you reach out to touch the key a chill runs up your spine and you make note of a small housing along the key’s handle that looked like it could fit a small gem – or perhaps a pearl. You carefully place the pearl with gloved hands into the housing and observe as the pearl takes on a sickly green glow. You realize that this key, and whatever magic it may possess, will guide you to Kur’zul.

You and your forces muster outside the walls of your outpost, unsure of what this key might do, and take a brief moment to breathe. This minute or so of unspoken agreement to savor the sunlight and fresh air around you calms you as you prepare to channel magical energy into the key to take you and your cohort to wherever it is Kur’zul has fled. Every moment of strife, chaos, deceit, and death on the island since you arrived to establish your outpost has led to this. “Duster… whatever might happen, wherever it is we might go, I wish to thank you for allowing me to fight alongside you,” Thaddius says solemnly, forcing a smile. “The Triptych owes you a great deal and they don’t even know it yet,” he says before turning his attention to the key. “Now… let’s put down a necromancer.”

As you hold the key and focus on the pearl within, you feel the latent magical energies of the island channel through you and into the key, causing it to shudder gingerly in your hand before it bursts forward from your hand. It floats idly a few feet ahead of you before reality itself seems to split in half and a portal is formed. You cannot see what lies beyond, nor is the portal anything like the portals wizards of the Triptych have opened but you know that, as you and your troupe sally forth, this could be the last moment you ever stand on Myora.

Much like the gateway to the Realm of Chaos, as you step through the portal you are left in a place entirely unfamiliar and eerie. You stand at the center of an immense, marble-hewn, promenade open on all sides with marble pillars suspending a marble ceiling. Beyond the edges of the promenade is an endless expanse of grey clouds without a sign of rain or storm as if wherever you were was an incomplete place. There are no sounds to be heard besides the pounding of your heart and heavy breathing of Thaddius at your side. The only thing of note was a thick, white, mist that could reach your calves that parted inexplicably, as if colliding with an invisible wall, to form a thin path forward through the plaza-like space towards a somewhat smaller building which looked like a sort of church or temple. The white building you approach is inlaid with long veins of gold seemingly crafted to appear like veins running through the pillars on the outside and the floors beneath your feet. It feels like they are feeding into a heart somewhere deeper inside. As you slowly move forward, out of the corner of your eye you spot some sort of writhing in the thick mist but whatever force field keeps the mist from your path seems to stop whatever stalks you. Down a short set of stairs and through an entryway obscured by shadow, the building opens up to a nearly empty room save for an immense, golden, altar being tended by someone at the center and a tall throne beyond where a figure lounged, enshrouded by a shimmering and shifting that made it impossible to tell who or what they are. The mist thickens as you enter the great chamber, though it still does not flood down into your path which leads to the altar and the throne beyond. The altar in the middle is the place that all the gold inlaid through the structure feeds into and, tending to it, preparing for some kind of ritual, is Kur’zul. A handful of robed liches, withered masters of the black-robed necromancers you cut down in the crypt, kneel in a ring around him.

The necromancer turns to peer at you over his shoulder. “You… You do not belong here,” he says almost plainly, as if he is bored and stating a fact. “I have worked for a century to get here. To stand in the hallowed halls of Kargral’s Temple. To unravel the tapestry of life and death. You will not stop me,” Kur’zul continues as he turns slowly to face you. His fingertips glow with an eerie, aqua-colored, flame which you know to be the same coldflame he threw at you in the fortress ruins. The figure lounging in the throne beyond the pathway seems to move in a very slow and deliberate manner as it stands to observe, which seems to cause Kur’zul to worry somewhat. “This is the one, great Khan, I spoke of. This is your vessel,” the necromancer says with heavy reverence in his tone. The form, perhaps Kargral if Kur’zul is to be believed, does not speak or respond in any way to Kur’zul but seemingly shifts its left arm and the clouds of mist that were barred by some invisible barrier cascade down into the path. Whatever protects you from the beasts in the mist now fades and the scaly, slithering, beasts worm their way closer towards you. High above the pillars comes the familiar beat of leathery wings: the green dragon that carried Kur’zul away from the fortress has followed its master even here. You ready your weapons and, beside you, Thaddius raises his sword and shield in preparation for the battle. Those who came with you slowly turn to form a circle, with backs to each other, and brace for the final battle ahead.

The slithering creatures that burst up from the mist, the temple’s Ancient Guardians, appear something like smooth-scaled, ivory-colored oarfish the size of immense snakes and they prove to be as deadly quick as they are formidable. As the guardians, the liches, and the circling dragon strike out against your cohort and the necromancer prepares for some type of strike, your eyes meet with Thaddius and you two come to a wordless understanding as to what needs to happen. Thaddius swiftly whirls around to offer up support to those who held against the temple’s Ancient Guardians while you prepare to face Kur’zul. A wicked, toothy, grin crosses over the necromancer’s countenance as the dancing, blue, flames in between his left fingertips begin to intensify and then coalesce into a semisolid sapphire blaze in the shape of a fiery sword while his right hand remains open to continue to channel those chilled flames. He dives forward to meet you in combat and the two of you begin to exchange blow after blow, dodging or blocking each other’s attacks with matched mastery.

Kur’zul grunts and growls with frustration and confoundment as you meet his attacks with defense and capitalize on openings to harm him when you can. By simply fighting him here, in this place beyond physical places, you drain his resolve and morale. In fury and frustration Kur’zul’s fiery magics grow less accurate as he becomes desperate to incinerate you. Each of his physical attacks becomes more furious and without form and you begin to feel the icy burn of the coldflame blade’s embers on your face as the blade seems to fall apart in his grasp. Finally with one powerful overhead strike, the Orc seeks to end you, but with a block, be it with blade or staff or bow, you meet his blade and it shatters into a million icy shards that burst out in a piercing, shrill, screech that seems to silence the whole realm. The force of the blow causes you to stagger backwards and lose your footing, falling, as Kur’zul recoils backwards. By the time you’ve regained your senses, the Orc looms ahead of you and is only a moment away from unleashing a fierce torrent of coldflame and ending you here and now when, in almost the blink of an eye, an armor-clad wall stands between you and the lethal spell with a loud cry in a voice you recognize well. “FOR MYORA!” Thaddius roars with a fury you’ve never heard from him as a sea of the necromancer’s deadly magic cascades from his palms to meet the mithril shield and armored form of Thaddius. The sapphire fire consumes your ally as he screams out in agony, the torrent burning through his armor and shield, and he begins to crumble before you though his valiance was not in vain. As he collapses before you Kur’zul’s great magical exertion causes a lapse in his reaction time and you scramble forward to capitalize on it by taking up Thaddius’ dropped sword and plunging it into the necromancer’s chest. As you sink the blade into the Orc’s heart he exhales a low groan, an exhalation as if he had almost wanted this, and his eyes lock onto yours. For the briefest moment, so fleeting, you think you see a hint of regret. This is victory. You’ve won.

As Kur’zul slumps and then collapses down to the ground, the entire realm seems to quake and scream, and the slithering ivory Ancient Guardians of the temple suddenly freeze and curl up as if they’ve been poisoned, before falling completely silent moments later. The liches crumble to dust where they kneel and, somewhere above, the green dragon shrieks and flees into the grey. The shimmering, shifting, form you presume to be Khan Kargral shudders before teleporting to loom just over Kur’zul’s body and yourself. As it stands there with no perceptible features other than the vagueness of its form, you feel as though it’s staring down at you in some form of appraisement. A thousand voices then pierce the silence of the realm, all speaking in different languages and taking different forms, though one speaks louder than the rest.

“A vessel was promised and a vessel was provided, though weak and crumpled, as was the nature of my demand,” it states, a deep male voice hewn from gravel and mealy dirt. “You, who would slay my kin, have done me a service. For that I will banish you from this realm. When I return to your world you shall be the first set free of The Call’s corruption. This is our accord.”

Then, as swiftly as the form had appeared before you, it raises up what you perceive to be its arm and, in an instant, you no longer stand in Kargral’s Temple but instead feel the gentle, warm, caress of the sea breeze amongst the trees outside your outpost. The surviving troops that accompanied you into the realm manifest all around you as you collapse from exhaustion, blacking out.
